facts: **Mode** is the value with the most dots, or the tallest column.
A data set has **no mode** when no value occurs more often than the others. If all data values are equal, that value is the mode. A data set can also have more than one mode.
steps: Find the smallest and largest values and subtract to get the range.
Find the value that occurs most often — that is the mode.
To compare two displays, work out each one's range and mode.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The smallest value with a dot is $2$ and the largest is $7$.
$\text{Range}=7-2=5$ books.
The tallest stack is above $4$, with four dots. The mode is $4$ books.

Team A: Each value occurs once. No value occurs more often than the others, so there is no mode.
Team B: $2$ and $4$ each occur three times, more often than any other value. The modes are $2$ and $4$ goals.

$\begin{aligned}\text{Stall A range}&=9-1\\&=8\text{ cups}\\\text{Stall B range}&=7-3\\&=4\text{ cups}\\\text{Difference}&=8-4\\&=4\text{ cups}\end{aligned}$
Stall A's range is $4$ cups greater. Stall B has more consistent sales because its range is smaller.
Stall A has modes $4$ and $6$ cups: both stacks have three dots. Stall B has mode $6$ cups: its tallest stack has four dots.
Both stalls include mode $6$, but Stall A also has mode $4$. Sharing a mode does not mean their ranges are equal.

workedExamples.question_text:
Four groups recorded the number of points scored in games.
A: $12,18,15,20,14$
B: $8,11,22,16,9$
C: $14,14,15,16,16$
D: $17,17,17,17,17$
Calculate each range. Which group has the greatest spread? Which group has the most consistent scores? Also find Group D's mode.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}\text{A range}&=20-12=8\\\text{B range}&=22-8=14\\\text{C range}&=16-14=2\\\text{D range}&=17-17=0\end{aligned}$
Group B has the greatest spread because its range is largest, $14$ points.
Group D has the most consistent scores because its range is $0$: all its scores are equal. Its mode is $17$ points, which occurs five times.

mastery.question_text:
Dataset A is $2,3,3,4,4,4,5,7$.
Dataset B is $1,4,4,4,6,6,8$.
A student says the displays have the same range and mode.
Evaluate the claim.
mastery.solution_text:
A range: $7-2=5$; A mode: $4$
B range: $8-1=7$; B mode: $4$
The modes match, but the ranges do not, so the claim is false.

Runner A range: $13.4-12.2=1.2$ seconds; modes: $12.5$ and $13.1$ seconds, each occurring twice.
Runner B range: $13.6-11.9=1.7$ seconds; mode: $12.5$ seconds, occurring three times.
Both include mode $12.5$ seconds, but Runner A also has mode $13.1$ seconds. Runner A is more consistent because the range is smaller.

Set R range: $25.8-21.4=4.4$ seconds; modes: $22.6$ and $24.1$ seconds.
Set S range: $25.3-20.9=4.4$ seconds; mode: $23.2$ seconds.
The claim is false. The ranges are equal, and Set S's mode lies between Set R's two modes.
